deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.1). M is a category in which (i) every arrow is a monomorphism and (ii) every endomorphism is the identity. N is the set of isomorphism classes of objects, preordered by the existence of a morphism. It is actually a poset: if D→D' and D'→D, both composites are endomorphisms, hence identities. For each n in N fix a representative D_n, unique up to unique isomorphism by (ii). Let J_n = \tilde D_n be the poset of subobjects of D_n.

This page.
(1) The 'type map' T_n : J_n → N sends a subobject to its isomorphism class. It is canonical and strictly increasing. If Δ' ⊂ Δ are subobjects of the same type, an isomorphism Δ ≅ Δ' composed with the inclusion gives an endomorphism of Δ. By (ii) that endomorphism is the identity, so Δ' = Δ.
(2) The image of T_n is N_{≤n} = {n' ≤ n}.
(3) J_n has a largest element d_n (D_n itself), and T_n^{-1}(n) = {d_n}. Any mono D_n → D_n is an endomorphism, hence the identity, by (ii).
(4) For n' ≤ n, the map Hom(D_{n'},D_n) → J_n, u ↦ u(d_{n'}), is injective and has image J_{n,n'} := T_n^{-1}(n'), the subobjects of type n'. Injectivity holds because two monos with the same image differ by an automorphism of D_{n'}, which is trivial.
(5) Each u : D_{n'} → D_n induces an order-preserving map on subobject posets, J_{n'} → J_n (direct image). This gives ρ_{n,n'} : J_{n,n'} → Hom(J_{n'},J_n), ξ ↦ u^n_ξ. It is injective because evaluation at d_{n'} recovers ξ; that is, the composite J_{n,n'} → Hom(J_{n'},J_n) → J_n is the inclusion.

Next page. u_ξ is an isomorphism J_{n'} ≅ (J_n)_{≤ξ}, and u_{d_n} = id. Composition must satisfy u^n_ξ u^{n'}_η = u^n_ζ with ζ = u^n_ξ(η). The data (N, J_n, T_n, ρ_{n,n'}) then reconstruct a skeleton M_0 of M: objects are N, morphisms are the 'admissible' poset maps.

Purpose. This is a combinatorial encoding of a loop-free category whose arrows are all monos (Δ_inj, face categories of regular cell complexes, posets) by graded families of posets with type functions. Presumably it prepares 'models' for the stack constructions in this dossier.

Modern reading. A 'loop-free category with monos' (an acyclic category / scwol in which all arrows are monic, akin to a direct category), described by its poset of objects together with the slices (subobject posets) and their gluing data.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. Hom(J_{n'},J_n) should be read as order-preserving maps.

The bijection Hom(D_{n'},D_n) ≅ T_n^{-1}(n') silently uses both (i) and (ii): images are subobjects by (i), and injectivity needs trivial automorphisms by (ii). Grothendieck only cites (i),(ii) on the previous page.
Finiteness or well-foundedness of N is not assumed. This is harmless here, since only N_{≤n} enters.

ideas.what: Category with all arrows mono and only identity endomorphisms; its isomorphism classes form a poset; it is determined up to equivalence by its skeleton.
ideas.modern_name: loop-free / acyclic category (scwol) with monic arrows; direct-category-like

ideas.what: Type map T_n : Sub(D_n) → N, strictly increasing, with image N_{≤n} and unique top element.
ideas.modern_name: rank/type function on a face poset (graded by the object poset)

ideas.what: Hom(D_{n'},D_n) ≅ subobjects of D_n of type n'; each morphism is an isomorphism J_{n'} ≅ (J_n)_{≤ξ}; reconstruction of the skeleton from (N, J_n, T_n, ρ).
ideas.modern_name: description of a category via slice/subobject posets; skeleton reconstruction

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, correct bookkeeping: encoding a skeletal loop-free category of monos by its object poset and subobject posets with type maps. Standard folklore; no novel result or connection is visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: The ℕ throughout should be N, the poset of isomorphism classes defined on p.1, not the natural numbers. Likewise 'ℕ_{≤n}' is N_{≤n} = {n' ∈ N | n' ≤ n}.
'une application conséquence' is very likely 'une application canonique, strictement croissante'.
Margin '$T_n$, application type' = 'T_n, application type' (type map).
The parenthetical reads roughly: 'qui est D_n lui-même (sous-objet maximal de D_n), et qui est noté d_n'. The '(par (ii))' justifies T_n^{-1}(n) = {d_n}.
Under the ρ arrow: '[≃ Hom(D_{n'},D_n)] ens des éléments de J_n de type n''.
